source_grounding.call_chain_traced: WRITE: PUT /collections/{name} JSON body -> CreateCollection (collection_meta_ops.rs:109, vectors: VectorsConfig, serde default, no deny_unknown_fields) -> VectorsConfig::Single(VectorParams) (types.rs:1470) -> VectorParams (types.rs:1338) declares only size/distance/hnsw_config/quantization_config/on_disk/datatype/multivector_config — the unknown JSON key 'memory' is silently dropped by serde for ANY value ('hot','pinned','cached') -> toc/create_collection.rs:20 proceeds; default-fill logic touches only on_disk -> 200 {result:true,status:ok}. READBACK: GET /collections/{name} -> CollectionInfo.config CollectionConfig (types.rs:166) -> params: CollectionParams -> vectors: VectorsConfig -> same VectorParams serialization (skip_serializing_if on optional fields) -> vectors JSON contains only {size,distance,...} — config.params.vectors.memory can NEVER appear. One mechanism explains all three observed behaviors (hot-200, pinned-200, cached-200-with-None-readback). Same-family contrast (code-level, not a live probe): the adjacent declared field on the very same struct, on_disk, IS persisted and echoed, which localizes the drop to the absent field rather than to whole-vectors-config leniency.

mundane_explanation.surviving: doc/code divergence for 1.18.x: the constraint's [SPEC] text (and the script's R8 spec-grid cross-check) say the versioned v-1-18-x api-reference documents a memory enum {cold,cached,pinned}, while the v1.18.0 source implements no such parameter at all (docs describing a feature the binary never had, or the constraint over-specified for this version). My direct verification of the nested doc schema was blocked (Fern render collapse; /openapi.json returns a selector page; contract source_verified=false), so whether the versioned page truly documents memory for 1.18.x is unconfirmed. This surviving explanation is the auditor's decision point: if the doc does document memory for 1.18.x, the silent drop of a documented enum parameter (accepting out-of-enum 'hot' and dense-unsupported 'pinned' with flat 200s, and never echoing even the legal 'cached') is a genuine spec violation; if the doc does not, the constraint is ungrounded for this version. The source-side fact (parameter entirely absent, silently ignored, no by-design annotation) holds either way.
